raw.details:
Event Details

  • Date: 23 October 2026
  • Time: 12:00 PM – 1:30 PM
  • Venue: Volleyball Court, I.T.S Engineering College, Greater Noida
  • Registration Fee: ₹300/team
  • Prize Pool: ₹12,000
  • Coordinator: Mr. Deepak Kumar Prajapati

Event Description

Senior Robo Sumo is a robotics challenge at TechTrix'26 where teams compete using RC-controlled robots in a sumo-style arena. The objective is to push the opponent's robot completely out of the ring while demonstrating robot control, mechanical design, maneuverability, and strategy. Participants bring a ready-to-compete robot and battle it out in a single-elimination knockout format.

Guidelines

Team Size & Eligibility

  • 2 participants per team; each team brings its own RC-controlled robot
  • Open to eligible undergraduate/postgraduate students and participants from colleges/institutions
  • Valid institutional/college ID is mandatory
  • Only registered participants may compete; one participant cannot be registered in two teams for the same event
  • Team composition cannot be changed after the registration deadline without Event Coordinator approval

Robot Specifications

Specification Requirement
Maximum Dimensions 350 × 350 mm (L × B)
Maximum Weight 3 kg
Maximum Voltage 3S LiPo, 12V DC/3s (fully charged)
Control Fully wireless, manual control only — autonomous robots strictly prohibited
Power Onboard power source (no external power during the match)
Propulsion Wheels, tracks, or legs only — hovercrafts/flying robots not allowed
Prohibited IC engines, compressors, weapons, sharp edges, explosive/corrosive/hazardous materials

Pre-Event Inspection

  • Teams must report to the arena at least 30 minutes before the official start time
  • Every robot undergoes a mandatory technical inspection and weigh-in; a robot that fails to meet the specifications will be disqualified before the match begins

Arena & Competition Format

  • Circular sumo ring, approximately 1.5–2 metres in diameter, with a smooth surface
  • Single-elimination knockout format; a full bracket will be drawn and displayed before matches begin, with byes (for uneven team counts) assigned via random draw
  • Each match is a direct 1v1 battle, with robots starting from designated positions in the ring
  • A robot is "out" the moment any part of it touches the floor outside the ring
  • Each match lasts a maximum of 5 minutes
  • A robot that loses power or stops functioning mid-match is automatically disqualified from that match, and the opponent advances

Judging Criteria

If neither robot is eliminated within the 5-minute time limit, the judges determine the advancing winner based on:

  • Aggression — which robot consistently initiated attacks or pushes
  • Strategy — effectiveness of tactics used to push the opponent or avoid being pushed
  • Control — which robot maintained the best control of its movements and positioning

Disqualification

The following will result in disqualification:

  • Exceeding the published dimensions, weight, or voltage limit
  • Using a wired controller or autonomous operation
  • Robots or mechanisms carrying weapons, sharp edges, or hazardous materials
  • Receiving unauthorized external assistance
  • Deliberately damaging the arena or another participant's equipment
  • Cheating or attempting to manipulate the competition
  • Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, foul/abusive language, unsportsmanlike conduct, harassment, or intentional/reckless damage to campus property or the arena

The Event Jury/Referee/Technical Committee holds final authority on robot eligibility, technical inspection, match decisions, penalties, disqualification, safety decisions, and rule interpretation. Right to appeal: a penalized team may present its case to the Judge and Event Coordinators, but the final verdict rests entirely with the organizers.

NOTE-: Registration Fees are not refundable.
